# Sources

<!-- Generated by tools/docs.ts from data/sources.yaml. Do not edit: change the data and run `pnpm docs`. -->

Every source Phosphoros cites, with the date someone last checked that the link works and says what we
cite it for. To add one, open an ["add a source" issue](https://github.com/Xaxis/phosphoros.space/issues/new?template=add-a-source.yml).

## Data

- <a id="nasa-venus-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Venus Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/venusfact.html). Checked 2026-11-21.<br>Mass, radius, orbit (with its J2000 inclination and ascending node), atmosphere mass and composition, surface temperature and pressure, rotation.
- <a id="nasa-earth-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Earth Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nasa-mercury-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Mercury Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/mercuryfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nasa-jupiter-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Jupiter Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Jupiter's mass, semi-major axis and perihelion.
- <a id="nasa-sun-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Sun Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nist-co2"></a>National Institute of Standards and Technology. [NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69: Carbon dioxide, phase change data](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C124389&Mask=4). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Critical point 304.13 K and 73.77 bar, heat capacity, the heat of deposition and the heats of reaction. Its triple point, 216.58 K and 5.185 bar, agrees with the Span and Wagner values the model uses.
- <a id="jpl-sbdb-ceres"></a>NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics. [JPL Small-Body Database: 1 Ceres](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/tools/sbdb_lookup.html#/?sstr=1). Checked 2026-11-23.<br>Ceres's semi-major axis, aphelion, eccentricity, inclination, ascending node, argument of perihelion, mean anomaly and mean motion (J2000 ecliptic, osculating at JD 2461200.5, JPL solution of 13 April 2021).
- <a id="standish-1992-approx"></a>Standish, E. M., and Williams, J. G. (NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics). [Approximate Positions of the Planets](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html). Checked 2026-11-23.<br>Keplerian elements of the planets and their rates, for 1800 to 2050 (Table 1); the mean longitudes of Mercury, Venus and Earth at J2000 and their rates, and Mercury's eccentricity and perihelion.
- <a id="tuv-x-spectra"></a>NCAR Atmospheric Chemistry Observations and Modeling (2024). [TUV-x photolysis model, input data: O₃ and O₂ cross-sections and extraterrestrial solar spectra](https://github.com/NCAR/TUV-x/tree/main/test/data/old_tuv/DATAE1). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The files in data/spectra/: O₃ cross-sections from JPL Publication 06-2 (Sander et al. 2006); O₂'s Herzberg continuum from Yoshino et al. (1988), Planetary and Space Science 36, 1469; sunlight from ATLAS-3 SUSIM (1994) below 400 nm and from Neckel and Labs (1984), Solar Physics 90, 205, above.
- <a id="toray-t1100g"></a>Toray Composite Materials America (2025). [TORAYCA T1100G Intermediate Modulus Carbon Fiber, technical data sheet (Rev. 11/24/2025)](https://www.toraycma.com/wp-content/uploads/T1100G-Data-Sheet.pdf). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Tensile strength 7,000 MPa and density 1.79 g/cm³; sizes the Aegis coil's structure.

## Papers and books

- <a id="iau-2015-nominal"></a>Mamajek, E. E., Prsa, A., Torres, G., et al. (2015). [IAU 2015 Resolution B3 on Recommended Nominal Conversion Constants for Selected Solar and Planetary Properties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07674). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Nominal solar radius and luminosity.
- <a id="kopp-lean-2011"></a>Kopp, G., and Lean, J. L. (2011). [A new, lower value of total solar irradiance: Evidence and climate significance](https://doi.org/10.1029/2010GL045777). Geophysical Research Letters 38, L01706. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The solar constant at Earth, 1,361 W/m².
- <a id="codata-2018"></a>Tiesinga, E., Mohr, P. J., Newell, D. B., and Taylor, B. N. (2021). [CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2018](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025010). Reviews of Modern Physics 93, 025010. [Free copy](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/archive2018.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The 2022 adjustment leaves every constant we use unchanged at the precision we use.
- <a id="span-wagner-1996"></a>Span, R. and Wagner, W. (1996). [A New Equation of State for Carbon Dioxide Covering the Fluid Region from the Triple-Point Temperature to 1100 K at Pressures up to 800 MPa](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.555991). Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data 25, 1509. [Free copy](https://srd.nist.gov/jpcrdreprint/1.555991.pdf). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The triple point, 216.592 K and 0.51795 MPa; the melting-pressure correlation, Eq. 3.10 (a₁ = 1955.5390, a₂ = 2055.4593); and the sublimation-pressure correlation, Eq. 3.12 (a₁ = −14.740846, a₂ = 2.4327015, a₃ = −5.3061778), which meets the vapour curve at the triple point.
- <a id="park-2016-ceres"></a>Park, R. S., Konopliv, A. S., Bills, B. G., et al. (2016). [A partially differentiated interior for (1) Ceres deduced from its gravity field and shape](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature18955). Nature 537, 515 to 517. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Ceres's mass, mean radius and rotation period from Dawn.
- <a id="gladman-1993"></a>Gladman, B. (1993). [Dynamics of systems of two close planets](https://doi.org/10.1006/icar.1993.1169). Icarus 106, 247 to 263. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Two bodies on near-circular orbits never meet if their orbits stay more than 2√3 mutual Hill radii apart, the clearance the model asks of Ceres's new orbit and Jupiter's.
- <a id="hamilton-burns-1991"></a>Hamilton, D. P. and Burns, J. A. (1991). [Orbital stability zones about asteroids](https://doi.org/10.1016/0019-1035(91)90039-V). Icarus 92, 118 to 131. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Prograde orbits around an asteroid stay bound out to about half its Hill radius, the test the model applies to the Crown.
- <a id="ceres-water"></a>McCord, T. B., and Sotin, C. (2005). [Ceres: Evolution and current state](https://doi.org/10.1029/2004JE002244). Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets 110, E05009. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Ceres's density suggests 17 to 27% water by mass. This estimate predates the Dawn mission; the model's 27% is the top of that range and the program's "40% of Ceres's water" depends on it. Post-Dawn interior models (Ermakov et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/2017JE005302) are the next source to check.
- <a id="basalt-thermal"></a>Robertson, E. C. (1988). [Thermal properties of rocks](https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr88441). U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 88-441. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Dense basalt conducts about 2.0 W/(m·K) by extrapolated measurement and 2.55 W/(m·K) calculated from its minerals. The model uses 2.5, the upper value, which slightly overstates crust heat flow.
- <a id="smrekar-2023-heatflow"></a>Smrekar, S. E., Ostberg, C., and O'Rourke, J. G. (2023). [Earth-like lithospheric thickness and heat flow on Venus consistent with active rifting](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41561-022-01068-0). Nature Geoscience 16, 13 to 18. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="ei-statistical-review"></a>Energy Institute (2025). [Statistical Review of World Energy 2025](https://www.energyinst.org/statistical-review). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Global primary energy of about 590 EJ in 2024, an average of 1.9 × 10¹³ W.
- <a id="stull-1947"></a>Stull, D. R. (1947). [Vapor Pressure of Pure Substances. Organic and Inorganic Compounds](https://doi.org/10.1021/ie50448a022). Industrial and Engineering Chemistry 39, 517 to 540. [Free copy](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7446095&Mask=4). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Sulfur dioxide's vapour pressure, as Antoine coefficients the NIST Chemistry WebBook fits to Stull's data from 177.7 K to 263 K (A = 3.48586, B = 668.225 K, C = −72.252 K, pressure in bar).
- <a id="coquelet-2014"></a>Coquelet, C., and Arpentinier, P. (2014). [Thermodynamic study of binary and ternary systems containing CO2 + impurities in the context of CO2 transportation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fluid.2014.08.031). Fluid Phase Equilibria 382, 205 to 211. [Free copy](https://trc.nist.gov/ThermoML/10.1016/j.fluid.2014.08.031.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Measured vapour-liquid equilibrium of CO₂ + SO₂ at 263.15 K and 333.21 K. At 263.15 K the pure SO₂ boils at 104.1 kPa, and a liquid with 0.103 SO₂ by mole is in equilibrium at 2349.5 kPa with a vapour holding 0.0147 SO₂.
- <a id="baines-2021"></a>Baines, K. H., Nikolić, D., Cutts, J. A., and others (2021). [Investigation of Venus Cloud Aerosol and Gas Composition Including Potential Biogenic Materials via an Aerosol-Sampling Instrument Package](https://doi.org/10.1089/ast.2021.0001). Astrobiology 21, 1316 to 1323. [Free copy](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:be4638a6-adf7-41a3-ab15-26ef6cce2d38/files/rkh04dq22w). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>From Knollenberg and Hunten's Pioneer Venus particle data: over the cloud column from 46 to 70 km the aerosol burden is 22 mg/cm² (0.22 kg/m²), droplets of sulfuric acid from 70% to 99% by weight.
- <a id="sagan-1961"></a>Sagan, C. (1961). [The Planet Venus](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.133.3456.849). Science 133, 849 to 858. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="adelman-1982"></a>Adelman, S. J. (1982). [Can Venus be transformed into an Earth-like planet?](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1982JBIS...35....3A/abstract). Journal of the British Interplanetary Society 35, 3. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>End page not confirmed; no DOI exists.
- <a id="birch-1991"></a>Birch, P. (1991). [Terraforming Venus Quickly](https://www.orionsarm.com/fm_store/TerraformingVenusQuickly.pdf). Journal of the British Interplanetary Society 44, 157 to 167. - <a id="cooke-2022"></a>Cooke, G. J., Marsh, D. R., Walsh, C., Black, B., and Lamarque, J.-F. (2022). ## Law and policy

- <a id="iau-2012-au"></a>International Astronomical Union (2012). [IAU 2012 Resolution B2: re-definition of the astronomical unit of length](https://www.iau.org/IAU/Iau/Publications/List-of-Resolutions.aspx). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The astronomical unit is exactly 149,597,870,700 m. The list gives Resolution B2 under the 2012 General Assembly; the version 2 link to the General Assemblies page now returns 404.
- <a id="outer-space-treaty"></a>United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (1967). [Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies](https://www.unoosa.org/unoosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Article II bars national appropriation; Article IX requires avoiding harmful contamination.
- <a id="cospar-pp"></a>Committee on Space Research. [COSPAR Policy on Planetary Protection](https://cosparhq.cnes.fr/cospar-policy-on-planetary-protection/). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="enmod"></a>United Nations (1976). [Convention on the Prohibition of Military or Any Other Hostile Use of Environmental Modification Techniques (ENMOD)](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XXVI-1&chapter=26&clang=_en). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Adopted on 10 December 1976, in force since 5 October 1978. Article II covers any technique that changes the dynamics, composition or structure of the earth or of outer space; Article I bans their hostile use, and Article III leaves peaceful use free.
